explanation: The V82A mutation reduces a bulky hydrophobic side chain to a smaller methyl group, creating a ~51 Ų cavity in the protease binding pocket that atazanavir normally occupies through van der Waals contacts. This loss of favorable hydrophobic packing at the 3.3 Å interface destabilizes the inhibitor's binding geometry, particularly disrupting the optimized van der Waals envelope that atazanavir relies on for tight binding in this critical subpocket. The reduced hydrophobicity (Δ-2.4) further weakens the desolvation penalty compensation that normally drives inhibitor binding, collectively accounting for the ~0.9 kcal/mol binding penalty.
